visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The scene opens in a brightly lit indoor living room where six people are seated on a gray sofa against a plain white wall. A central female figure with vibrant orange hair and large yellow hoop earrings is the focal point, wearing a white cutout top and a yellow skirt with a plush Winnie the Pooh character on her lap. To her left, two females sit, and to her right, another female, while three males sit behind them. The central figure gestures with her hand as white and blue text overlays appear on the screen. (2) The video transitions through several cuts showing various group members' reactions. A male in a black hoodie and beanie smiles broadly, while another female with long dark hair holds a purple cushion and laughs. The lighting is consistent and bright studio-style, illuminating facial expressions clearly. Text overlays in Korean characters and English phrases like 'It's Beautiful Life' appear prominently at the bottom and center of the frame. (3) The camera uses frequent medium shots and occasional digital zoom-ins on individual faces to emphasize their comedic expressions. One female in a denim jacket leans forward, speaking with an animated facial expression. In some segments, cartoon-style graphic overlays, such as flames, a supermarket icon, or a character from South Park, are placed over the subjects' faces or in the background to enhance the variety-show aesthetic. (4) The group continues to interact dynamically, with several members covering their faces while laughing or pointing at each other. The central orange-haired woman remains the lead, frequently looking directly at the camera. The editing is fast-paced with many jump cuts that follow the flow of the conversation, and colored horizontal bars briefly flicker on the screen as a stylistic transition toward the end.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: To entertain viewers through a humorous group challenge where participants attempt to sing Korean song lyrics by phonetically translating them into funny Chinese phrases. The core appeal lies in the comedic failure of the singers and the genuine group laughter that follows.
